# Question: 
The senior developer has been on this codebase for 3 years. He thinks test automation is overhead — when something breaks, he fixes it from memory in 20 minutes. He's not hostile, but he doesn't believe QA adds value. How do you get him to care about quality without being condescending? Not a generic 'build trust' answer. What specifically would you say or do in your first week?

# Answer:


Since he is Senior he does know about his own codebase and how its work.
i Will give some key Points why QA is important like :

- I will what problems consume most of his time. I will give a small test suite of basic smoke/regression testing to show him how its save time by not testing but to invest time in fixing.

- As the application grows, modules become more connected. A change in one module can affect payroll, attendance, or employee management without anyone realizing it.

- QA perpspective is different where developer test only happy path but Test Engineer tests the application in order to break the system.

- Test Automation helps in repetative task if the System is small deeveloper can perform and test every e2e functionality but the more module add the more complex code means more changes of bugs.
